result.title: PlaceTally: A Test-Time Memory Model for Constructing Place Graphs
result.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Code, data and supplementary material: https://alibayosmanli.github.io/placetally
result.summary: Counting distinct objects in a video is hard when the camera returns to places it has seen. A vision-language model that reads the whole video answers with a few small numbers, and one that reads it in parts counts an object again in every part that shows it. Object trackers need the category before the video is read, or a fixed vocabulary. We observe that a memory for counting does not need to know what it is looking for, only where it has been: objects rarely leave a room between visits, so parts of a video grouped by place share almost no objects, and a place can be recognised before any question is asked. Building on this, we introduce PlaceTally, a question-blind test-time memory model that constructs a place graph for each video. Each video fragment joins the place of its best earlier match or opens a new place, because a strong match is rarely wrong while a true return often matches weakly. A frozen vision-language model counts each place once from at most 128 of its frames, so every read has a bounded input and the memory grows with the number of places; the graph is built 15 times faster than real time. On RevisitCount, our benchmark of real room re-recordings, it scores 62.5% mean relative accuracy on test rooms and 61.2% on held-out rooms, against 51.2% and 44.3% for the same model reading the whole video. It stays level as rooms return more or less often, while a fixed correction of summed visits moves from 38.5% to 61.4%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PlaceTally：一个 question-blind 的测试时记忆模型，为每段视频构建 place graph，每个片段并入最佳历史匹配的地点或新建地点，再由冻结 VLM 对每个地点最多读 128 帧完成计数，并在真实房间重录基准 RevisitCount 上超过整段视频读取。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「匹配强度决定复用已有状态还是新建状态」及定长帧读取带来的有界证据输入与缓存管理，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、状态更新和计算预算分配提供可核查的结构线索，但论文本身不涉及 latent 表示或推理轨迹。
